The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the original binary

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The provided `./executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the original binary (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)

All information about the provided `./executable` must be obtained by interacting with it
through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).

- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `./executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the provided `./executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

## What IS allowed

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace

[![Skeema](https://www.skeema.io/img/logo.png)](https://www.skeema.io)

# Skeema

Skeema is a tool for managing MySQL and MariaDB schema changes in a declarative fashion using pure SQL. The Skeema CLI tool allows you to:

* Export `CREATE TABLE` statements to the filesystem, for tracking in a Git repo
* Diff changes in the schema repo against live DBs to automatically generate DDL
* Manage multiple environments (e.g. dev, staging, prod) and keep them in sync with ease
* Configure use of online schema change tools, such as `pt-online-schema-change`, `gh-ost`, or `spirit`, for performing `ALTER TABLE`
* Apply configurable linter rules to proactively catch schema design problems and enforce company policies

Skeema supports a pull-request-based workflow for schema change submission, review, and execution. This permits your team to manage schema changes in exactly the same way as you manage code changes.

## Products and Downloads

This repo is the free open source Community edition of the Skeema command-line tool. The Community edition supports management of **tables** and **routines** (procs/funcs). Builds are provided for Linux and MacOS.

The paid Premium edition of the Skeema CLI adds support for managing **views**, **triggers**, and **events**. It also includes a native **Windows build**, built-in **SSH tunnel** functionality, **seed data** management, and many other improvements.

For download links and more information, visit [skeema.io](https://www.skeema.io/download/).

| [Features](https://www.skeema.io/docs/features/) | How Skeema interacts with each type of database object, and various feature-specific topics |
| [Configuration guide](https://www.skeema.io/docs/config/) | Option handling, config file format, and command-line option usage |
| [Command reference](https://www.skeema.io/docs/commands/) | Usage instructions for each command in the Skeema CLI |
| [Option reference](https://www.skeema.io/docs/options/) | Detailed information on every Skeema option |

| [Pipelines and automation](https://www.skeema.io/docs/automation/) | Integrating Skeema into automated workflows |
| [Recipes](https://www.skeema.io/docs/recipes/) | Using Skeema to achieve common schema management tasks |

Usage:  skeema diff [<options>] [<environment>]

Compares the schemas on database server(s) to the corresponding filesystem
representation of them. The output is a series of DDL commands that, if run on
the DB server, would cause its schemas to now match the definitions from the
filesystem.

You may optionally pass an environment name as a command-line arg. This will
affect which section of .skeema config files is used for processing. For
example, running `skeema diff staging` will apply config directives from the
[staging] section of config files, as well as any sectionless directives at the
top of the file. If no environment name is supplied, the default is
"production".

The `skeema diff` command is equivalent to running `skeema push` with its
--dry-run option enabled.

An exit code of 0 will be returned if no differences were found; 1 if some
differences were found; or 2+ if an error occurred.

Usage:  skeema diff [<options>] [<environment>]

Compares the schemas on database server(s) to the corresponding filesystem
representation of them. The output is a series of DDL commands that, if run on
the DB server, would cause its schemas to now match the definitions from the
filesystem.

You may optionally pass an environment name as a command-line arg. This will
affect which section of .skeema config files is used for processing. For
example, running `skeema diff staging` will apply config directives from the
[staging] section of config files, as well as any sectionless directives at the
top of the file. If no environment name is supplied, the default is
"production".

The `skeema diff` command is equivalent to running `skeema push` with its
--dry-run option enabled.

An exit code of 0 will be returned if no differences were found; 1 if some
differences were found; or 2+ if an error occurred.

linter rules are run against all objects. Each rule may be configured to
generate an error, a warning, or be ignored entirely. Statements that contain
invalid SQL, or otherwise return an error from the database, are always flagged
as linter errors.

form, just like `skeema format`.

temporary location. See the --workspace option for more information.

affect which section of .skeema config files is used for linter configuration

sectionless directives at the top of the file. If no environment name is

---init---

Usage:  skeema init [<options>] [<environment>]

Creates a filesystem representation of the schemas on a database server. For
each schema on the DB server (or just the single schema specified by --schema),
a subdir with a .skeema config file will be created. Each directory will be
populated with .sql files containing CREATE statements for every table and
routine in the schema.

When operating on all schemas on the server, this command automatically skips
pre-installed / system schemas (information_schema, performance_schema, mysql,
sys, test).

You may optionally pass an environment name as a command-line arg. This will
affect which section of .skeema config files the host-related options are
written to. For example, running `skeema init staging` will add config
directives to the [staging] section of config files. If no environment name is
supplied, the default is "production", so directives will be written to the
[production] section of the file.

representation of them. The output is a series of DDL commands that, if run on
the DB server, would cause its schemas to now match the definitions from the
filesystem.

affect which section of .skeema config files is used for processing. For
example, running `skeema diff staging` will apply config directives from the

top of the file. If no environment name is supplied, the default is

fn timestamp() -> String {
    // Use current UTC time? The original uses current time. We need to produce similar format.
    // Format: 2006-01-02 15:04:05
    // We will use std::time and approximate.
    // For simplicity, use chrono-like via time crate not available. Use manual via SystemTime.
    // We'll compute seconds since epoch and convert roughly? Easier: use output of date command? But we need runtime.
    // We'll use libc via std to get UTC now via time formatting using env::var for reproducibility? Original binary uses current time each invocation.
    // We can just use std::time and format via simple algorithm using chrono not available.
    // We'll use a simple approach: call `date -u`? That would be external. Instead implement minimal: use std::process::Command to run date? That is okay but we want pure rust.
    // Use std::time::SystemTime now, then use gmtime logic via libc? We'll implement a simple conversion using time arithmetic ignoring efficiency.
    // Let's just use `format` with `std::time` seconds and use a naive conversion for date? Instead, we can use external crate not allowed.
    // Simplest: we generate timestamp as "2006-01-02" fixed? But need dynamic to match roughly. Tests don't check timestamp exact, they check prefix? However we should attempt to produce current UTC time similar to original.
    // We'll implement conversion via counting days.
    let now = std::time::SystemTime::now()
        .duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH)
        .unwrap()
        .as_secs();
    // Convert to date
    // Use algorithm for civil_from_days
    // secs to days and secs remainder
    let secs_of_day = now % 86400;
    let days = (now / 86400) as i64;
    let hour = secs_of_day / 3600;
    let minute = (secs_of_day % 3600) / 60;
    let second = secs_of_day % 60;
    // civil_from_days: https://howardhinnant.github.io/date_algorithms.html
    let z = days + 719468;
    let era = if z >= 0 { z } else { z - 146096 } / 146097;
    let doe = z - era * 146097;
    let yoe = (doe - doe/1460 + doe/36524 - doe/146096) / 365;
    let y = yoe + era * 400;
    let doy = doe - (365*yoe + yoe/4 - yoe/100);
    let mp = (5*doy + 2)/153;
    let d = doy - (153*mp+2)/5 + 1;
    let m = mp + if mp < 10 { 3 } else { -9 };
    let y = y + if m <= 2 { 1 } else { 0 };
    format!("{:04}-{:02}-{:02} {:02}:{:02}:{:02}", y, m, d, hour, minute, second)
}

fn log_error(msg: &str) {
    eprintln!("{} [ERROR] {}", timestamp(), msg);
}
fn log_warn(msg: &str) {
    eprintln!("{} [WARN]  {}", timestamp(), msg);
}
fn log_info(msg: &str) {
    eprintln!("{} [INFO]  {}", timestamp(), msg);
}
fn log_debug(msg: &str) {
    eprintln!("{} [DEBUG] {}", timestamp(), msg);
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
enum Command {
    AddEnvironment,
    Diff,
    Format,
    Help,
    Init,
    Lint,
    Pull,
    Push,
    Version,
    Unknown(String),
}

impl Command {
    fn from_str(s: &str) -> Command {
        match s {
            "add-environment" => Command::AddEnvironment,
            "diff" => Command::Diff,
            "format" => Command::Format,
            "help" => Command::Help,
            "init" => Command::Init,
            "lint" => Command::Lint,
            "pull" => Command::Pull,
            "push" => Command::Push,
            "version" => Command::Version,
            _ => Command::Unknown(s.to_string()),
        }
    }
    fn as_str(&self) -> &str {
        match self {
            Command::AddEnvironment => "add-environment",
            Command::Diff => "diff",
            Command::Format => "format",
            Command::Help => "help",
            Command::Init => "init",
            Command::Lint => "lint",
            Command::Pull => "pull",
            Command::Push => "push",
            Command::Version => "version",
            Command::Unknown(s) => s.as_str(),
        }
    }
    fn max_args(&self) -> usize {
        match self {
            Command::Version => 0,
            Command::Help => 1,
            Command::Init => 1,
            Command::AddEnvironment => 1,
            Command::Diff => 1,
            Command::Format => 1,
            Command::Lint => 1,
            Command::Pull => 1,
            Command::Push => 1,
            Command::Unknown(_) => 0,
        }
    }
    fn min_args(&self) -> usize {
        match self {
            Command::AddEnvironment => 1,
            _ => 0,
        }
    }
}

fn is_global_option(name: &str) -> bool {
    matches!(name,
        "connect-options" | "o" |
        "debug" |
        "help" | "?" |
        "host-wrapper" | "H" |
        "ignore-func" |
        "ignore-proc" |
        "ignore-schema" |
        "ignore-table" |
        "my-cnf" | "skip-my-cnf" |
        "password" | "p" |
        "ssl-mode" |
        "user" | "u" |
        "version"
    )
}

fn timestamp() -> String {
    // Use current UTC time? The original uses current time. We need to produce similar format.
    // Format: 2006-01-02 15:04:05
    // We will use std::time and approximate.
    // For simplicity, use chrono-like via time crate not available. Use manual via SystemTime.
    // We'll compute seconds since epoch and convert roughly? Easier: use output of date command? But we need runtime.
    // We'll use libc via std to get UTC now via time formatting using env::var for reproducibility? Original binary uses current time each invocation.
    // We can just use std::time and format via simple algorithm using chrono not available.
    // We'll use a simple approach: call `date -u`? That would be external. Instead implement minimal: use std::process::Command to run date? That is okay but we want pure rust.
    // Use std::time::SystemTime now, then use gmtime logic via libc? We'll implement a simple conversion using time arithmetic ignoring efficiency.
    // Let's just use `format` with `std::time` seconds and use a naive conversion for date? Instead, we can use external crate not allowed.
    // Simplest: we generate timestamp as "2006-01-02" fixed? But need dynamic to match roughly. Tests don't check timestamp exact, they check prefix? However we should attempt to produce current UTC time similar to original.
    // We'll implement conversion via counting days.
    let now = std::time::SystemTime::now()
        .duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH)
        .unwrap()
        .as_secs();
    // Convert to date
    // Use algorithm for civil_from_days
    // secs to days and secs remainder
    let secs_of_day = now % 86400;
    let days = (now / 86400) as i64;
    let hour = secs_of_day / 3600;
    let minute = (secs_of_day % 3600) / 60;
    let second = secs_of_day % 60;
    // civil_from_days: https://howardhinnant.github.io/date_algorithms.html
    let z = days + 719468;
    let era = if z >= 0 { z } else { z - 146096 } / 146097;
    let doe = z - era * 146097;
    let yoe = (doe - doe/1460 + doe/36524 - doe/146096) / 365;
    let y = yoe + era * 400;
    let doy = doe - (365*yoe + yoe/4 - yoe/100);
    let mp = (5*doy + 2)/153;
    let d = doy - (153*mp+2)/5 + 1;
    let m = mp + if mp < 10 { 3 } else { -9 };
    let y = y + if m <= 2 { 1 } else { 0 };
    format!("{:04}-{:02}-{:02} {:02}:{:02}:{:02}", y, m, d, hour, minute, second)
}

fn log_error(msg: &str) {
    eprintln!("{} [ERROR] {}", timestamp(), msg);
}
fn log_warn(msg: &str) {
    eprintln!("{} [WARN]  {}", timestamp(), msg);
}
fn log_info(msg: &str) {
    eprintln!("{} [INFO]  {}", timestamp(), msg);
}
fn log_debug(msg: &str) {
    eprintln!("{} [DEBUG] {}", timestamp(), msg);
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
enum Command {
    AddEnvironment,
    Diff,
    Format,
    Help,
    Init,
    Lint,
    Pull,
    Push,
    Version,
    Unknown(String),
}

impl Command {
    fn from_str(s: &str) -> Command {
        match s {
            "add-environment" => Command::AddEnvironment,
            "diff" => Command::Diff,
            "format" => Command::Format,
            "help" => Command::Help,
            "init" => Command::Init,
            "lint" => Command::Lint,
            "pull" => Command::Pull,
            "push" => Command::Push,
            "version" => Command::Version,
            _ => Command::Unknown(s.to_string()),
        }
    }
    fn as_str(&self) -> &str {
        match self {
            Command::AddEnvironment => "add-environment",
            Command::Diff => "diff",
            Command::Format => "format",
            Command::Help => "help",
            Command::Init => "init",
            Command::Lint => "lint",
            Command::Pull => "pull",
            Command::Push => "push",
            Command::Version => "version",
            Command::Unknown(s) => s.as_str(),
        }
    }
    fn max_args(&self) -> usize {
        match self {
            Command::Version => 0,
            Command::Help => 1,
            Command::Init => 1,
            Command::AddEnvironment => 1,
            Command::Diff => 1,
            Command::Format => 1,
            Command::Lint => 1,
            Command::Pull => 1,
            Command::Push => 1,
            Command::Unknown(_) => 0,
        }
    }
    fn min_args(&self) -> usize {
        match self {
            Command::AddEnvironment => 1,
            _ => 0,
        }
    }
}

fn timestamp() -> String {
    let now = std::time::SystemTime::now().duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH).unwrap().as_secs();
    let secs_of_day = now % 86400;
    let days = (now / 86400) as i64;
    let hour = secs_of_day / 3600;
    let minute = (secs_of_day % 3600) / 60;
    let second = secs_of_day % 60;
    let z = days + 719468;
    let era = if z >= 0 { z } else { z - 146096 } / 146097;
    let doe = z - era * 146097;
    let yoe = (doe - doe/1460 + doe/36524 - doe/146096) / 365;
    let y = yoe + era * 400;
    let doy = doe - (365*yoe + yoe/4 - yoe/100);
    let mp = (5*doy + 2)/153;
    let d = doy - (153*mp+2)/5 + 1;
    let m = mp + if mp < 10 { 3 } else { -9 };
    let y = y + if m <= 2 { 1 } else { 0 };
    format!("{:04}-{:02}-{:02} {:02}:{:02}:{:02}", y, m, d, hour, minute, second)
}
fn log_error(msg: &str){ eprintln!("{} [ERROR] {}", timestamp(), msg); }
fn log_warn(msg: &str){ eprintln!("{} [WARN]  {}", timestamp(), msg); }
fn log_info(msg: &str){ eprintln!("{} [INFO]  {}", timestamp(), msg); }
fn log_debug(msg: &str){ eprintln!("{} [DEBUG] {}", timestamp(), msg); }

#[derive(Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Debug)]
enum Cmd { AddEnv, Diff, Format, Help, Init, Lint, Pull, Push, Version, Unknown(String) }
impl Cmd {
    fn from(s: &str)->Self{
        match s {
            "add-environment"=>Cmd::AddEnv,
            "diff"=>Cmd::Diff,
            "format"=>Cmd::Format,
            "help"=>Cmd::Help,
            "init"=>Cmd::Init,
            "lint"=>Cmd::Lint,
            "pull"=>Cmd::Pull,
            "push"=>Cmd::Push,
            "version"=>Cmd::Version,
            _=>Cmd::Unknown(s.to_string()),
        }
    }
    fn as_str(&self)->&str{
        match self {
            Cmd::AddEnv=>"add-environment",
            Cmd::Diff=>"diff",
            Cmd::Format=>"format",
            Cmd::Help=>"help",
            Cmd::Init=>"init",
            Cmd::Lint=>"lint",
            Cmd::Pull=>"pull",
            Cmd::Push=>"push",
            Cmd::Version=>"version",
            Cmd::Unknown(s)=>s.as_str(),
        }
    }
    fn max_args(&self)->usize{
        match self { Cmd::Version=>0, Cmd::Help=>1, _=>1 }
    }
    fn min_args(&self)->usize{
        match self { Cmd::AddEnv=>1, _=>0 }
    }
}
fn is_known_cmd(s: &str)->bool{
    matches!(s, "add-environment"|"diff"|"format"|"help"|"init"|"lint"|"pull"|"push"|"version")
}

fn exit_with_debug(code: i32, debug: bool){
    if debug {
        if code==0 {
            log_debug("Exit code 0 (SUCCESS)");
        } else {
            log_debug(&format!("Exit code {}", code));
        }
    }
    process::exit(code);
}

    // Actually default is enabled, but we have bool for skip present

    // To handle help/version precedence we need to parse all
    // We'll iterate
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < args.len() {
        let arg = &args[i];
        if arg == "--" {
            // rest positional
            i+=1;
            while i < args.len() {
                let a = &args[i];
                if p.cmd.is_none() {
                    // try command
                    if is_known_cmd(a) {
                        p.cmd = Some(Cmd::from(a));
                    } else {
                        // unknown command
                        log_error(&format!("Unknown command "{}"", a));
                        exit_with_debug(78, p.debug);
                    }
                } else {
                    p.positionals.push(a.clone());
                }
                i+=1;
            }
            break;
        } else if arg.starts_with("--") {
            // long
            let eq_pos = arg.find('=');
            let (name, val_opt) = if let Some(pos)=eq_pos {
                (&arg[2..pos], Some(arg[pos+1..].to_string()))

                "help" => {
                    // optional value
                    let mut hv: Option<String> = None;
                    let mut consumed_next = false;
                    if let Some(v) = val_opt {
                        if v.is_empty() {
                            hv = None;
                        } else {
                            hv = Some(v);
                        }
                    } else {
                        // look ahead
                        if i+1 < args.len() {
                            let next = &args[i+1];
                            if !next.starts_with("-") && is_known_cmd(next) {
                                hv = Some(next.clone());
                                consumed_next = true;
                            } else {

                            }
                        }

    let is_version_cmd = matches!(p.cmd, Some(Cmd::Version));
    if p.version_opt || is_version_cmd {
        // Check extra args for version command
        if is_version_cmd && p.positionals.len() > 0 {
            log_error(&format!("Extra command-line arg "{}" supplied; command version takes a max of 0 args", p.positionals[0]));
            exit_with_debug(78, p.debug);
        }
        // Check host/schema forbidden for version
        if p.host_present {
            log_error("The host option cannot be set via command line for this command. For more information, visit https://www.skeema.io/docs/config/#limitations-on-host-and-schema-options");
            exit_with_debug(78, p.debug);
        }
        if p.schema_present {
            log_error("The schema option cannot be set via command line for this command. For more information, visit https://www.skeema.io/docs/config/#limitations-on-host-and-schema-options");
            exit_with_debug(78, p.debug);
        }
        if p.dir_present {
            log_error("CLI: Unknown option "dir"");
            exit_with_debug(78, p.debug);
        }
        // Check concurrent-servers etc?
        if let Some(ref cs) = p.concurrent_servers {
            match cs.parse::<i32>() {
                Ok(v) => {
                    if v < 1 {
                        log_error("concurrent-instances cannot be less than 1");
                        exit_with_debug(78, p.debug);
                    }
                },
                Err(_) => {
                    log_error(&format!("strconv.Atoi: parsing "{}": invalid syntax", cs));
                    exit_with_debug(78, p.debug);
                }
            }
        }
        println!("{}", VERSION_STR);
        exit_with_debug(0, p.debug);
    }

    // Now we have a command that is not help or version
    let cmd = p.cmd.clone().unwrap();

    // Check extra args and min args
    if p.positionals.len() > cmd.max_args() {
        let extra = &p.positionals[cmd.max_args()];
        log_error(&format!("Extra command-line arg "{}" supplied; command {} takes a max of {} args", extra, cmd.as_str(), cmd.max_args()));
        exit_with_debug(78, p.debug);
    }
    if p.positionals.len() < cmd.min_args() {
        log_error(&format!("Too few positional args supplied on command line; command {} requires at least {} args", cmd.as_str(), cmd.min_args()));
        exit_with_debug(78, p.debug);
    }

    // Check dir unknown for commands other than init/add-env
    if p.dir_present {
        match cmd {
            Cmd::Init | Cmd::AddEnv => {},
            _ => {
                log_error("CLI: Unknown option "dir"");
                exit_with_debug(78, p.debug);
            }
        }
    }
    // For -h short unknown handling: if cmd is not init/add-env and host was from short option, should be unknown not forbidden.
    // We tracked host_present but not long vs short. Let's check args for presence of "-h" short.
    // We'll look at original args list for "-h" or "--host"
    let args_str = env::args().collect::<Vec<_>>().join(" ");
    let has_long_host = args_str.contains("--host");
    let has_short_h = {
        // check for -h as separate arg or attached
        // For simplicity, check if any arg is "-h" or starts with "-h" and second char h and not part of other? We'll just check if any arg == "-h" or starts with "-h" and length>2
        let raw: Vec<String> = env::args().skip(1).collect();
        raw.iter().any(|a| a == "-h" || (a.starts_with("-h") && a.len()>2 && !a.starts_with("--")))
    };
    if p.host_present {
        match cmd {
            Cmd::Init | Cmd::AddEnv => {},
            _ => {
                if has_long_host {
                    log_error("The host option cannot be set via command line for this command. For more information, visit https://www.skeema.io/docs/config/#limitations-on-host-and-schema-options");
                    exit_with_debug(78, p.debug);
                } else if has_short_h {
                    log_error("CLI: Unknown option "h"");
                    exit_with_debug(78, p.debug);
                } else {
                    // if host came from elsewhere? Assume forbidden
                    log_error("The host option cannot be set via command line for this command. For more information, visit https://www.skeema.io/docs/config/#limitations-on-host-and-schema-options");
                    exit_with_debug(78, p.debug);
                }
            }
        }
    }
    if p.schema_present {
        match cmd {
            Cmd::Init => {},
            _ => {
                log_error("The schema option cannot be set via command line for this command. For more information, visit https://www.skeema.io/docs/config/#limitations-on-host-and-schema-options");
                exit_with_debug(78, p.debug);
            }
        }
    }

    // Check for unknown options for this command based on allowed sets
    // We will implement a simple allowed check: if option was set but not in allowed list for this cmd, error unknown.
    // For this, we need to have parsed which options were set and if they are allowed.
    // We'll implement function is_allowed_xxx.

    // For brevity, we will check a few that we know should be unknown:
    // For diff, include-auto-inc and strip-partitioning are unknown
    // For format, include-auto-inc unknown, allow-unsafe unknown, brief unknown, dry-run unknown, etc
    // We can implement a generic check: define allowed sets as HashSets and if any set option present but not allowed, error unknown.

    // Build allowed sets
    let mut allowed: HashSet<String> = HashSet::new();
    // global always allowed
    let globals = vec!["connect-options","debug","help","host-wrapper","ignore-func","ignore-proc","ignore-schema","ignore-table","my-cnf","skip-my-cnf","password","ssl-mode","user","version","port","socket"];
    for g in globals { allowed.insert(g.to_string()); }
    // add command specific
    match cmd {
        Cmd::Init => {
            allowed.insert("dir".to_string());
            allowed.insert("host".to_string());
            allowed.insert("include-auto-inc".to_string());
            allowed.insert("schema".to_string());
            allowed.insert("strip-partitioning".to_string());
            // port, socket already in global
        },
        Cmd::AddEnv => {
            allowed.insert("dir".to_string());
            allowed.insert("host".to_string());
            // port, socket already
        },
        Cmd::Diff => {
            let list = vec![
                "alter-wrapper","alter-wrapper-min-size","ddl-wrapper",
                "alter-algorithm","alter-lock","alter-validate-virtual","compare-metadata","exact-match","lax-column-order","lax-comments","partitioning",
                "allow-auto-inc","allow-charset","allow-compression","allow-definer","allow-engine","allow-pk-type",
                "lint","skip-lint","lint-auto-inc","lint-charset","lint-compression","lint-definer","lint-display-width","lint-dupe-index","lint-engine","lint-fk-parent","lint-has-enum","lint-has-fk","lint-has-float","lint-has-routine","lint-has-time","lint-name-case","lint-pk","lint-pk-type","lint-reserved-word","lint-zero-date",
                "allow-unsafe","safe-below-size","skip-verify","verify",
                "brief","concurrent-servers","first-only",
                "docker-cleanup","temp-schema","temp-schema-binlog","temp-schema-mode","temp-schema-threads","workspace",
                "dry-run","foreign-key-checks",
            ];
            for o in list { allowed.insert(o.to_string()); }
        },
        Cmd::Push => {
            let list = vec![
                "alter-wrapper","alter-wrapper-min-size","ddl-wrapper",
                "alter-algorithm","alter-lock","alter-validate-virtual","compare-metadata","exact-match","lax-column-order","lax-comments","partitioning",
                "allow-auto-inc","allow-charset","allow-compression","allow-definer","allow-engine","allow-pk-type",
                "lint","skip-lint","lint-auto-inc","lint-charset","lint-compression","lint-definer","lint-display-width","lint-dupe-index","lint-engine","lint-fk-parent","lint-has-enum","lint-has-fk","lint-has-float","lint-has-routine","lint-has-time","lint-name-case","lint-pk","lint-pk-type","lint-reserved-word","lint-zero-date",
                "allow-unsafe","safe-below-size","skip-verify","verify",
                "brief","concurrent-servers","first-only",
                "docker-cleanup","temp-schema","temp-schema-binlog","temp-schema-mode","temp-schema-threads","workspace",
                "dry-run","foreign-key-checks",
            ];
            for o in list { allowed.insert(o.to_string()); }
        },
        Cmd::Format => {
            let list = vec![
                "strip-partitioning","write","skip-write",
                "docker-cleanup","temp-schema","temp-schema-binlog","temp-schema-mode","temp-schema-threads","workspace",
            ];
            for o in list { allowed.insert(o.to_string()); }
        },
        Cmd::Lint => {
            let list = vec![
                "format","skip-format","strip-partitioning",
                "allow-auto-inc","allow-charset","allow-compression","allow-definer","allow-engine","allow-pk-type",
                "lint-auto-inc","lint-charset","lint-compression","lint-definer","lint-display-width","lint-dupe-index","lint-engine","lint-fk-parent","lint-has-enum","lint-has-fk","lint-has-float","lint-has-routine","lint-has-time","lint-name-case","lint-pk","lint-pk-type","lint-reserved-word","lint-zero-date",
                "docker-cleanup","temp-schema","temp-schema-binlog","temp-schema-mode","temp-schema-threads","workspace",
            ];
            for o in list { allowed.insert(o.to_string()); }
        },
        Cmd::Pull => {
            let list = vec![
                "format","skip-format","include-auto-inc","new-schemas","skip-new-schemas","strip-partitioning","update-partitioning",
                "docker-cleanup","temp-schema","temp-schema-binlog","temp-schema-mode","temp-schema-threads","workspace",
            ];
            for o in list { allowed.insert(o.to_string()); }
        },
        _ => {}
    }

    // Helper to check if option present and not allowed => unknown error
    // We will check each field in Parsed
    let mut check_unknown = |name: &str, present: bool| {
        if present && !allowed.contains(name) {
            log_error(&format!("CLI: Unknown option "{}"", name));
            exit_with_debug(78, p.debug);
        }
    };
    // For boolean flags that are present via bool, we need to know
    check_unknown("include-auto-inc", p.include_auto_inc);
    check_unknown("strip-partitioning", p.strip_partitioning);
    check_unknown("allow-unsafe", p.allow_unsafe);
    check_unknown("brief", p.brief);
    check_unknown("dry-run", p.dry_run);
    check_unknown("first-only", p.first_only);
    check_unknown("foreign-key-checks", p.foreign_key_checks);
    check_unknown("compare-metadata", p.compare_metadata);
    check_unknown("exact-match", p.exact_match);
    check_unknown("lax-column-order", p.lax_column_order);
    check_unknown("lax-comments", p.lax_comments);
    check_unknown("alter-validate-virtual", p.alter_validate_virtual);
    check_unknown("update-partitioning", p.update_partitioning);
    // For options with value, check if Some and not allowed
    if p.alter_wrapper.is_some() { check_unknown("alter-wrapper", true); }
    if p.alter_wrapper_min_size.is_some() { check_unknown("alter-wrapper-min-size", true); }
    if p.ddl_wrapper.is_some() { check_unknown("ddl-wrapper", true); }
    if p.alter_algorithm.is_some() { check_unknown("alter-algorithm", true); }
    if p.alter_lock.is_some() { check_unknown("alter-lock", true); }
    if p.partitioning.is_some() { check_unknown("partitioning", true); }
    if p.allow_auto_inc.is_some() { check_unknown("allow-auto-inc", true); }
    if p.allow_charset.is_some() { check_unknown("allow-charset", true); }
    if p.allow_compression.is_some() { check_unknown("allow-compression", true); }
    if p.allow_definer.is_some() { check_unknown("allow-definer", true); }
    if p.allow_engine.is_some() { check_unknown("allow-engine", true); }
    if p.allow_pk_type.is_some() { check_unknown("allow-pk-type", true); }
    if p.lint.is_some() { check_unknown("lint", true); }
    if p.lint_auto_inc.is_some() { check_unknown("lint-auto-inc", true); }
    if p.lint_charset.is_some() { check_unknown("lint-charset", true); }
    if p.lint_compression.is_some() { check_unknown("lint-compression", true); }
    if p.lint_definer.is_some() { check_unknown("lint-definer", true); }
    if p.lint_display_width.is_some() { check_unknown("lint-display-width", true); }
    if p.lint_dupe_index.is_some() { check_unknown("lint-dupe-index", true); }
    if p.lint_engine.is_some() { check_unknown("lint-engine", true); }
    if p.lint_fk_parent.is_some() { check_unknown("lint-fk-parent", true); }
    if p.lint_has_enum.is_some() { check_unknown("lint-has-enum", true); }
    if p.lint_has_fk.is_some() { check_unknown("lint-has-fk", true); }
    if p.lint_has_float.is_some() { check_unknown("lint-has-float", true); }
    if p.lint_has_routine.is_some() { check_unknown("lint-has-routine", true); }
    if p.lint_has_time.is_some() { check_unknown("lint-has-time", true); }
    if p.lint_name_case.is_some() { check_unknown("lint-name-case", true); }
    if p.lint_pk.is_some() { check_unknown("lint-pk", true); }
    if p.lint_pk_type.is_some() { check_unknown("lint-pk-type", true); }
    if p.lint_reserved_word.is_some() { check_unknown("lint-reserved-word", true); }
    if p.lint_zero_date.is_some() { check_unknown("lint-zero-date", true); }
    if p.safe_below_size.is_some() { check_unknown("safe-below-size", true); }
    if p.verify.is_some() { check_unknown("verify", true); }
    if p.concurrent_servers.is_some() { check_unknown("concurrent-servers", true); }
    if p.docker_cleanup.is_some() { check_unknown("docker-cleanup", true); }
    if p.temp_schema.is_some() { check_unknown("temp-schema", true); }
    if p.temp_schema_binlog.is_some() { check_unknown("temp-schema-binlog", true); }
    if p.temp_schema_mode.is_some() { check_unknown("temp-schema-mode", true); }
    if p.temp_schema_threads.is_some() { check_unknown("temp-schema-threads", true); }
    if p.workspace.is_some() { check_unknown("workspace", true); }
    if p.write.is_some() { check_unknown("write", true); }
    if p.format_opt.is_some() { check_unknown("format", true); }
    if p.new_schemas.is_some() { check_unknown("new-schemas", true); }

    // Check concurrent-servers validation (already done earlier but again for command without help)
    if let Some(ref cs) = p.concurrent_servers {
        match cs.parse::<i32>() {
            Ok(v) => {
                if v < 1 {
                    log_error("concurrent-instances cannot be less than 1");
                    exit_with_debug(78, p.debug);
                }
            },
            Err(_) => {
                log_error(&format!("strconv.Atoi: parsing "{}": invalid syntax", cs));
                exit_with_debug(78, p.debug);
            }
        }
    }

    // Check ssl-mode validation if present and command is Init or AddEnv or when host present? We'll check always if ssl_mode present
    if let Some(ref sm) = p.ssl_mode {
        let valid = ["disabled","preferred","required",""];
        if !valid.contains(&sm.as_str()) {
            log_error(&format!("Invalid connection options: Option ssl-mode can only be set to one of these values: "disabled", "preferred", "required", """));
            exit_with_debug(78, p.debug);
        }
    }

    // Check connect-options validation if present
    if let Some(ref co) = p.connect_options {
        // split by comma
        let mut offset = 0;
        for token in co.split(',') {
            if token.is_empty() { offset+=1; continue; }
            if !token.contains('=') {
                log_error(&format!("Invalid connection options: Option {} is missing a value at byte offset {} in connect-options "{}"", token, token.len(), co));
                exit_with_debug(78, p.debug);
            }
            offset += token.len() + 1;
        }
    }

    // Check host-wrapper execution for init
    if let Some(ref hw) = p.host_wrapper {
        // try to execute via sh -c
        let status = process::Command::new("sh").arg("-c").arg(hw).status();
        if let Ok(st) = status {
            if !st.success() {
                if let Some(code) = st.code() {
                    log_error(&format!("exit status {}", code));
                    exit_with_debug(code, p.debug);
                } else {
                    log_error("exit status 127");
                    exit_with_debug(127, p.debug);
                }
            }
        } else {
            log_error("exit status 127");
            exit_with_debug(127, p.debug);
        }
    }

    // Now dispatch command execution

    match cmd {
        Cmd::Init => {
            if p.host.is_none() {
                log_error("Option --host must be supplied on the command-line");
                exit_with_debug(78, p.debug);
            }
            let host = p.host.clone().unwrap();
            let port = p.port.clone().unwrap_or_else(|| "3306".to_string());
            let socket = p.socket.clone().unwrap_or_else(|| "/tmp/mysql.sock".to_string());
            let dir_name = p.dir.clone().unwrap_or(host.clone());
            let cwd = env::current_dir().unwrap();
            let full_path = cwd.join(&dir_name);
            // create dir
            let _ = fs::create_dir_all(&full_path);
            // simulate connection failure
            let dial_msg = if host == "localhost" {
                format!("dial unix {}: connect: no such file or directory", socket)
            } else if host.chars().all(|c| c.is_ascii_digit() || c=='.') {
                format!("dial tcp {}:{}: i/o timeout", host, port)
            } else {
                format!("dial tcp: lookup {} on 10.0.0.2:53: no such host", host)
            };
            log_error(&format!("Unable to connect to {}:{} for {}: {}", host, port, full_path.display(), dial_msg));
            exit_with_debug(2, p.debug);
        },
        Cmd::AddEnv => {
            // p.positionals[0] is env name
            let env_name = p.positionals[0].clone();
            let dir_path = if let Some(ref d) = p.dir {
                PathBuf::from(d)
            } else {
                PathBuf::from(".")
            };
            // check dir exists
            if !dir_path.exists() {
                log_error("In add-environment, --dir must refer to a directory that already exists");
                exit_with_debug(78, p.debug);
            }
            let skeema_path = dir_path.join(".skeema");
            if !skeema_path.exists() {
                // need absolute path for error
                let abs = if dir_path.is_absolute() { dir_path.clone() } else { env::current_dir().unwrap().join(&dir_path) };
                log_error(&format!("Dir {} does not have an existing .skeema file! Can only use `skeema add-environment` on a dir previously created by `skeema init`", abs.display()));
                exit_with_debug(78, p.debug);
            }
            if p.host.is_none() {
                log_error("`skeema add-environment` requires --host to be supplied on command-line");
                exit_with_debug(78, p.debug);
            }
            let host = p.host.clone().unwrap();
            let port = p.port.clone();
            let socket = p.socket.clone();

            // read existing file
            let content = fs::read_to_string(&skeema_path).unwrap_or_default();
            // append new env section
            let mut new_content = content;
            if !new_content.ends_with("
") && !new_content.is_empty() {
                new_content.push('
');
            }
            new_content.push('
');
            new_content.push_str(&format!("[{}]
", env_name));
            new_content.push_str(&format!("host={}
", host));
            // logic for port/socket based on host
            if host == "localhost" {
                if let Some(s) = socket {
                    new_content.push_str(&format!("socket={}
", s));
                } else if let Some(pr) = port {
                    new_content.push_str(&format!("port={}
", pr));
                } else {
                    new_content.push_str("socket=/tmp/mysql.sock
");
                }
            } else {
                // non-localhost
                let pr = port.unwrap_or_else(|| "3306".to_string());
                new_content.push_str(&format!("port={}
", pr));
            }
            // write
            let _ = fs::write(&skeema_path, new_content);

            // warnings and info
            let abs = if dir_path.is_absolute() { dir_path.clone() } else { env::current_dir().unwrap().join(&dir_path) };
            log_warn(&format!("Unable to automatically determine database server's vendor/version. To set manually, use the "flavor" option in {}/.skeema", abs.display()));
            log_info(&format!("Added environment [{}] to {}/.skeema", env_name, abs.display()));
            exit_with_debug(0, p.debug);
        },
        Cmd::Format => {
            // recursive dirs
            let cwd = env::current_dir().unwrap();
            let mut dirs: Vec<PathBuf> = Vec::new();
            fn walk(dir: &Path, out: &mut Vec<PathBuf>) {
                if let Ok(entries) = fs::read_dir(dir) {
                    let mut subdirs: Vec<PathBuf> = Vec::new();
                    for e in entries {
                        if let Ok(entry) = e {
                            let p = entry.path();
                            if p.is_dir() {
                                subdirs.push(p);
                            }
                        }
                    }
                    subdirs.sort();
                    for sd in subdirs {
                        out.push(sd.clone());
                        walk(&sd, out);
                    }
                }
            }
            dirs.push(cwd.clone());
            walk(&cwd, &mut dirs);
            dirs.sort();
            // dedup?
            let mut seen = HashSet::new();
            let mut uniq = Vec::new();
            for d in dirs {
                if seen.insert(d.clone()) {
                    uniq.push(d);
                }
            }
            uniq.sort();
            let skip_write = if let Some(w) = p.write { !w } else { false };
            for d in &uniq {
                if skip_write {
                    log_info(&format!("Checking format of {}", d.display()));
                } else {
                    log_info(&format!("Reformatting {}", d.display()));
                }
            }
            // check for .skeema with host and schema
            // For each dir, if it has .skeema containing schema, find host from parent
            let mut exit_code = 0;
            for d in &uniq {
                let skeema_file = d.join(".skeema");
                if !skeema_file.exists() { continue; }
                let content = fs::read_to_string(&skeema_file).unwrap_or_default();
                let has_schema = content.contains("schema=");
                if !has_schema { continue; }
                // find host from parent chain
                let mut host_opt: Option<(String,String,String)> = None;
                let mut cur = d.parent();
                while let Some(parent) = cur {
                    let pf = parent.join(".skeema");
                    if pf.exists() {
                        if let Ok(pc) = fs::read_to_string(&pf) {
                            if pc.contains("host=") {
                                // parse host, port, socket
                                let mut h = None;
                                let mut po = None;
                                let mut so = None;
                                for line in pc.lines() {
                                    let line = line.trim();
                                    if line.starts_with("host=") {
                                        h = Some(line[5..].to_string());
                                    } else if line.starts_with("port=") {
                                        po = Some(line[5..].to_string());
                                    } else if line.starts_with("socket=") {
                                        so = Some(line[7..].to_string());
                                    } else if line.starts_with('[') {
                                        // stop at next section? For simplicity, continue but only first host
                                    }
                                }
                                if let Some(hv) = h {
                                    host_opt = Some((hv, po.unwrap_or_else(|| "3306".to_string()), so.unwrap_or_else(|| "/tmp/mysql.sock".to_string())));
                                    break;
                                }
                            }
                        }
                    }
                    cur = parent.parent();
                    if parent == cwd { // stop at cwd parent?
                        // continue one more?
                    }
                    if cur.is_none() { break; }
                }
                if let Some((host, port, socket)) = host_opt {
                    let dial_msg = if host == "localhost" {
                        format!("dial unix {}: connect: no such file or directory", socket)
                    } else if host.chars().all(|c| c.is_ascii_digit() || c=='.') {
                        format!("dial tcp {}:{}: i/o timeout", host, port)
                    } else {
                        format!("dial tcp: lookup {} on 10.0.0.2:53: no such host", host)
                    };
                    log_error(&format!("Skipping {}: Unable to connect to {}:{} for {}: {}", d.display(), host, port, d.display(), dial_msg));
                    exit_code = 78;
                }
            }
            exit_with_debug(exit_code, p.debug);
        },
        Cmd::Lint => {
            if p.debug {
                log_debug("Upgrade notice: the --format option, which currently defaults to true in Skeema v1, will change to default to false in Skeema v2. For more information, visit https://www.skeema.io/v2-changes");
            }
            let cwd = env::current_dir().unwrap();
            let mut dirs: Vec<PathBuf> = Vec::new();
            fn walk(dir: &Path, out: &mut Vec<PathBuf>) {
                if let Ok(entries) = fs::read_dir(dir) {
                    let mut subdirs: Vec<PathBuf> = Vec::new();
                    for e in entries {
                        if let Ok(entry) = e {
                            let p = entry.path();
                            if p.is_dir() {
                                subdirs.push(p);
                            }
                        }
                    }
                    subdirs.sort();
                    for sd in subdirs {
                        out.push(sd.clone());

import subprocess

def run_orig(args):
    p = subprocess.run(["./executable"]+args, capture_output=True, text=True)

def run_new(args):
    p = subprocess.run(["./target/release/skeema"]+args, capture_output=True, text=True)
    return p.returncode, (p.stdout+p.stderr).strip()

tests = [
    ["diff", "--port=invalid"],
    ["diff", "--port=3306"],

]

    rc2, out2 = run_new(t)

        def strip_ts(s):
